newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia SBI eases amid profit-taking, Dow falls.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia SBI eases amid profit-taking, Dow falls.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI share index closed 0.83 percent lower on Monday amid a lack of foreign demand, as sharp falls in key world markets triggered a bout of profit-taking, traders said.
"Domestic investors don't dare to invest when western foreigners are sitting on their hands," one trader said.
Wall Street clocked up the largest one-day point drop since October 1997 on Friday, rattling world stock markets.
But some traders say the falls have been more of a correction rather than the beginning of a bear market, despite some fears of monetary tightening in the U.S. or continental Europe.
The SBI index eased 0.83 percent or 13.26 points to 1,587.14. Overall 13 shares fell, four rose and one was flat while 10 were untraded. Turnover fell to 113.8 million tolars from 167.8 million.
Trading firm Kovinotehna, a favourite among small investors because of its three-digit price, was the most actively traded stock, falling 3.28 percent to 561 tolars on volume of 9,404 shares.
Petrol trader Petrol led decliners, falling 4.18 percent to 25,010 tolars on volume of 2,065 shares, worth 51.9 million tolars.

"Petrol was already a bit over-priced and I think it was down mainly due to technical reaction, but it is not likely to fall lower than 24,000. Many people also think Lek is over-priced, although I can't see it under 35,000," another broker said.
Drug maker Lek eased 1.69 percent to 36,070 tolars on volume of 458 shares.
Construction firm GPG was the top gainer, jumping 8.76 percent to 6,210 tolars on volume of 10 shares.
"GPG...is one of less liquid shares here so each purchase can move the share in either direction significantly," one trader said.
